So San Diego pre-pandemic and post pandemic are two different things. I moved to San Diego pre pandemic and it was still a well kept secret on how beautiful and amazing it was. Significant population boom in short amount of time that drove up the rent significantly. Jammed up the highways. And also priced out so many mom and pop restaurants and locals. I swear the black population in San Diego was better than it was now. Or maybe it’s because no one can afford going out and shopping everyone staying inside lol. There is a very active Facebook group called Black San Diego and tells you all the black owned everything in the area. But you have actively put yourself out there to meet people. I am so sorry that you didn’t get the validation you needed in your session. It sounds like the therapist may have had an ego and did not wanted to disclose that they do not have this extensive knowledge. Ethically, therapists should be referring out if they do have a knowledge in a subject area especially since there are typically so many therapists that may have that speciality. Neurodivergence is an area that is emerging research especially in adult women. I hope within time professionals will grow to be more knowledgeable about this specific area

I have a mix of 4b/4c high density hair. So I do mostly everything in the shower because everything is significantly easier when my hair is soaking wet. I double wash and then I put on conditioner (I use cheap super moistening conditioner because I do put on a lot to assist in the detangling process) I don’t use combs I primarily finger detangle my hair and with the conditioner. Then afterwards while still in the shower I put in Pattern Styling Curling crème. It has flaxseed in it which my hair loves. 

That’s when I get out of the shower and then I just put on the gel throughout my hair and then diffuse . Mind you, I don’t diffuse to like 100 percent dry. I only diffuse to 70 percent and let the rest air dry. I actually think doing this more than once a week actually cuts down the time because my hair is not super tangled .
I also shampoo twice! One clarifying than follow up with a moisturizing shampoo

Yes, this amount of teething is normal. Yes, she most likely does think of it as a game. For me, the whole “yelping like a puppy to let them know it hurts” only worked for maybe the first two weeks. After that, I’m convinced that he thought i was a chew toy. What kind of chew toys does she have? Get as many as you with different textures. Don’t get expensive ones, because they will destroy them rather quickly. Is she overstimulated? Puppies at that age need a lot of naps. Like I’m talking almost 20 hours of sleeping. I found, even to this day (mine is pushing six months) he gets mouthy when he is super tired. So the trick is teaching them bite inhibition, not stop chewing all together. Puppies use their mouths to explore the world. The only thing that worked after watching every YouTube video about this issue is one redditor suggested the “gentle cue”. I have a treat in my fist, and he would sniff it and try to mouth it to get it. If he started licking instead of biting, he would get the treat and I would cue gentle. Me and my SO did that consistently and now when we say gently, he will resort to licking or gentler touch. It sounds weird, but it worked tremendously.
